Mars Pathfinder drag coefficient traced back from the flight (validation/pathfinder/convert_pds.py)
# Reference length: 1.325 m
# CD = 2 m a/(rho A V^2) with a the measured axial acceleration (PDS r_sacc_s.tab), rho the
# reconstructed density (PDS edl_ddr.tab) and V the speed integrated from the entry state.
# This is the drag coefficient the NASA reconstruction used (Braun et al. 1995 database),
# along the path the vehicle flew. Separable form CD(Mach, Kn) = CD_c(Mach) + dCD(Kn):
# CD_c from the continuum part (Kn < 0.005), dCD from the rarefied part up to Kn 0.05,
# then a sin^2 bridge to the free-molecular 2 at Kn 10 (no flight data there).
# Mach = V/sqrt(gamma R T/M) with gamma 1.335, M 43.49 g/mol.
variables = Kn, CFx, CFy, CFz, CMx, CMy, CMz, SDV_CFx, SDV_CFy, SDV_CFz, SDV_CMx, SDV_CMy, SDV_CMz, Altitude
